title: Daily, Weekly, or Event-driven Doxycycline for STI Prevention Among Men Who Have Sex With Men (MSM) Engaging in Chemsex: The DOSE Non-inferiority Trial
official: Daily, Weekly, or Event-driven Doxycycline for STI Prevention Among Men Who Have Sex With Men (MSM) Engaging in Chemsex: The DOSE Non-inferiority Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if three different dosing strategies of doxycycline (daily, weekly, and on-demand) works to prevent sexually transmitted infections (gonorrhea, chlamydia, and syphilis) among men who use methamphetamine and who have sex with other men. The main question it aims to answer is:

Does daily, weekly, and on-demand doxycycline dosing strategies lower the incidence of quarterly STIs (gonorrhea, chlamydia, and syphilis)?

Participants will:

Take doxycycline either on-demand (within 72 hours after sex), daily, or weekly doxycycline for one year Visit the clinic once every 3 months to complete questionnaires, undergo HIV/STI testing, and collect samples. Additional visits may be needed to receive STI treatment.

Complete text surveys once every month
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Born male
* Age ≥ 18 years old
* Reports receiving an STI diagnosis (i.e., GC, CT, and/or syphilis) in the past 12 months
* Reports MA use in conjunction with CAI with a male partner in the 30 days prior to screening
* Not planning to relocate out of the study area in the 12-month follow-up period
* Willingness to engage in up to one year of repeated antibiotic exposure
* Willing and able to give written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Reported allergy to tetracyclines
* Current or anticipated use of a medication that interacts with doxycycline (prohibited medications listed below)
* Current or planned use of doxycycline for a prolonged period (\> 2 weeks, with the exception of pre-enrollment doxyPEP)
* Prolonged antibiotic use (\> 2 weeks, with the exception of pre-enrollment doxyPEP) in the 30 days prior to study enrollment
* Co-enrollment in any other concurrent study that may interfere with this study, such as an STI prevention trial, unless approved by the PI or designee
* Any other medical or psychiatric condition that, in the opinion of the PI or designee, may interfere with study participation or participant safety
